summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic foot ulcers from prior frostbite, was admitted for worsening left foot pain, swelling, and erythema despite two weeks of oral antibiotics. Imaging revealed osteomyelitis in the fourth and fifth toes, and he was admitted for IV antibiotic therapy and source control. He underwent podiatric debridement of the affected toes, and a PICC line was placed to complete a 14-day course of IV vancomycin and ciprofloxacin. His pain was managed with scheduled and breakthrough opioids, with plans to taper upon improvement. His cardiac medications were held initially due to hypotension but were restarted before discharge. He was transitioned to extended care for antibiotic completion and was discharged in stable condition with follow-up arranged in podiatry, cardiology, and primary care.
